name: DeLaurenti Roero Arneis DOCG
description:
Arneis is Piedmont’s native white, grown for centuries on the same hills that yield Barolo and Barbaresco. By the 1980s it had almost vanished, but a small band of growers nursed it back, and in the ’90s it re-emerged as Roero’s calling card - sometimes dubbed "Barolo bianco," though it needs no comparison to justify its place at the table.

This bottling comes from the sandy slopes of Santo Stefano Roero. It pours a bright straw yellow. The nose suggests fresh fruit and white flowers. On the palate it’s crisp and poised, with stone-fruit flavors giving way to a clean, mineral finish, typical of the Roero landscape.

Think of Arneis as a lively alternative to Sancerre or a Pinot Grigio with more nerve. Chill it lightly and pair with shellfish, grilled trout, or a simple roast chicken. It’s the sort of everyday white that makes summer meals feel complete.

name: Angiolino Maule Masieri Bianco
description: Angiolino Maule, a pioneer of natural winemaking in Italy, provides a delightful twist on Soave with his Masieri Bianco. Swirls of pear, citrus, and stone fruit are balanced by crisp acidity in this refreshing white wine. Our wine buyer, Tom Drake, says, “It’s like wine agua fresca. I love it.” This versatile Garganega-based gem pairs brilliantly with fresh salads, delicate seafood, or an afternoon by the pool.

name: Cardedu 'Nuo' Vermentino di Sardegna
description: Sardinian Vermentinos are known for their captivating balance of vivacity and depth, and this wine is no exception. The esteemed Cardedu estate delivers a quintessential example in this bright, citrusy Vermentino — Meyer lemon, tangerine zest, and delicate elderflower. A leesy texture adds complexity, while a touch of saline minerality lingers. The bright acidity makes it a versatile wine but we recommend it with grilled halibut or a plate of Linguine ai Frutti di Mare and pretending you’re dining al fresco on Sardinia’s sun-soaked, breezy coast.

name: Cirelli Vino da Tavola Bianco
description: Just because you're looking for an inexpensive, weeknight sort of wine, doesn't mean you should have to sacrifice flavor and quality. This wine blends Trebbiano and Pecorino (the grape, not to be confused with the cheese) for a light, snappy, refreshing white wine suitable for any occasion.

name: Cirelli Vino Orange
description:
Although orange wine may be having a moment, it isn't any more of a fad than white, red, or rosé wine. Despite its confusing name, the 'orange' in orange wine only refers to the color of the wine. You may also come across terms like amber wine or skin contact wine, and the three are synonymous. In order to make this style of wine, the winemaker leaves the white grape skins in contact with the grape juice for an extended period of time, like one does when making a red wine.

In this case, Cirelli macerates Trebbiano for about a month on its skins, followed by a soft pressing into stainless steel. What comes through in the bottle are subtle black tea tannins, a little bit of nectarine, and a mouth-watering, refreshing finish. This wine is sure to appease orange wine novices and afficianados alike!

name: Cor Cellars "Ago" Columbia Gorge Chardonnay
description: Cor makes several wines under the "Ago" label that highlight fruit from the Columbia Gorge. This is a dry, unoaked Chardonnay that shares a lot qualities with our favorite Alpine wines. Fittingly, this wine is great with all that Alpine cheese and Gouda in your basket, or with some PNW shellfish or salmon.

name: Domaine Billard Pere & Fils Bourgonge Blanc
description: Jerome Billiard brings a very holistic approach to the vineyard, eschewing the use of chemical fertilizers and plowing his rows with a horse. He allows the fruit to hang on the vine a little longer than most of his neighbors and allows his wines to ferment spontaneously, too, creating a Chardonnay here with a richer mouthfeel and concentration of fruit, without falling into the oaky and buttery side of things. This is a great wine for classic bistro fare - think roast chicken, hand-made sausages, and pates.

name: Domaine de Roally Viré-Clessé
description: From the Thévenet family, this organically farmed Viré-Clessé ranks among the finest wines of the Mâconnais. Made from late-harvested old-vine Chardonnay, the 2022 shows vibrant acidity and steely minerality balanced by flavors of yellow apple and saline. Very dry with vibrant acidity, the finish of this wine lingers like a Mid-west Goodbye. Delicious now yet structured to age a decade or more. Wines of this quality from more prestigious parts of Bourgogne go for five or six times this price. One of our favorite white wines in the entire store.

name: Fidora Pinot Grigio Venezia DOC
description: Brimming with character, this crisp Pinot Grigio hails from a vast biodynamic estate in northern Italy. Delightful and budget-friendly, it boasts an inviting medley of citrus, green apple, and pear flavors. Share a bottle with friends or pair it with a scrumptious meal – this versatile gem shines on any occasion, echoing the charm of its Amarone sibling.

name: Graci Etna Bianco
description: As is the case with most Etna Bianco, Graci primarily utilizes Carricante and a splash of Catarratto. In effect, these grapes portray qualities similar to Chablis or great wines made from Vernaccia. The fruit comes from several contrada on Etna's northern slope, and the finished product from these volcanic vines is a crisp, mineral-driven white wine perfect for lighter, seafood-based pasta dishes. It's also a treat with the bounty of PNW seafood we're privy to in Seattle, and its natural citrus and flint aromas complement oysters perfectly.

name: Kiona Vineyards Chardonnay
description: Our friends at Kiona, who helped our House Red come to life, make a lot of fantastic wines. If you're in the market for a local Chardonnay that leans towards the richer end of the spectrum with just a slightly noticeable amount of oak, this is definitely the wine for you!

name: Le Chai Duchet 'The Berry Story' Macon Blanc
description: Le Chai Duchet's refreshingly dry Chardonnay hails from Southern Burgundy, delivering a flourish of tropical notes alongside crisp apple, an intriguing hint of yeastiness, and chalky minerality. Winemaker Alexis Duchet farms his family’s Mâcon vineyards organically. Biodynamic farming is challenging for the grapes, but excellent for the wine. Duchet’s Mâcon Blanc pairs nicely with freshly grilled seafood or creamy chicken dishes, making it an enchanting companion for a languid summer lunch.

name: Le Coste 'Due M' Moscato
description: Le Coste is a beautiful estate in Lazio, just a little outside Rome. The Due M cuvee is a blend of Moscato from two different sites- theirs, which is a mix of old and young vines, and from a friend who farms in a like-minded fashion. Their fruit goes through carbonic maceration and the sourced fruit does not. The result is a tropical, textured, orange wine that is incredibly dissimilar to the sweet Moscato wines found in the north. A delicious substitute for a light-bodied red at the table, we love it with Carbonara and Cacio e Pepe.

name: Le Fontane 'Calcis' Bianco
description: Mediterranean white wines are so often a great choice because they present such versatility and approachability, especially considering the climate and cuisine of the Pacific Northwest. Le Fontane's 'Calcis' cuvée goes beyond simply being some "nice" choice, however, and excels when paired with halibut, shrimp, or other local shellfish. The wine is equal parts Grillo and Insolia, two grapes that bring equal parts wildflower and citrus-driven acidity, but there's also a splash of Malvasia in the blend that brings this gorgeous, tropical note to the front.

name: Le Monde Pinot Grigio
description: This Pinot Grigio from Friuli has all the bright, crisp fruit you'd expect and a mineral-driven, dry finish. A great daily-drinker to have on hand, this wine is also great with pesto-based pasta dishes or with some fresh panzanella.

name: Nanclares Y Prieto 'Dandelion' Albarino
description: This Spanish white wine has this citrus and saline quality to it that perfectly complements sheep's milk cheeses, briney tinned fish, and jamon. It's incredibly refreshing but with a richer profile that lingers with minerality and fresh lemon zest.

name: Ridge Estate Chardonnay
description: Silky elegance put California Chardonnay on the world map and this beauty by Ridge Estate is an exquisite example of just how good it can be. The winery embraces traditional winemaking and sustainability. This Chardonnay transcends oaky clichés, offering smooth sophistication that deftly balances soft, creamy pear and bright citrus notes. Pair it with a succulent roast chicken or buttery lobster risotto and settle into an evening of luxury.

name: Santola Vinho Verde
tagline: Vinho Verde DOC - Loureiro & Pederna - NV
description: This value-oriented gem hailing from Portugal's lush northwestern region is super fresh, bright, and slightly fizzy. Exhibiting vibrant notes of green apple, citrus, and subtle floral undertones, Santola Vinho Verde is suited for sipping solo or enjoying with friends, tapas, or appetizers. In a world where wine often takes itself too seriously, Santola Vinho Verde stands proud with an irreverent wink, an effervescent grin, and encourages you to raise a glass to the sheer delight of existence.

name: Savage Grace Columbia Gorge Chardonnay
description: From a Certified Organic Columbia Gorge vineyard, fermented in neutral French oak barrels. It offers refreshing acidity, minerality, medium body and intense flavors. Salmon? Yes. Food optional? Also yes.

name: Savage Grace Red Willow Vineyard Sauvignon Blanc
description: Savage Grace makes fantastic wines from fruit sourced from the Yakima Valley, Columbia Gorge, and Walla Walla. This Sauvignon Blanc comes from the famed Red Willow Vineyard and is the perfect bridge between Washington Sauvignon Blanc and Sancerre. Less melon and tropical fruit, a lot more minerality. Whether looking for local or imported wines, this is always a top choice for a seafood pairing.

name: Travis Tausend "Agori" Chardonnay
description: Aussie wines often get (unfairly) overlooked due to the American market being flooded with mass produced “not so great” wines from our friends down under. Let your mind erase those thoughts here and now with this amazing Chardonnay from young maverick, Travis Tausend. You can show off this “new world” beauty to your most discerning friends and discover the potential this region is flexing!

name: Via Alpina Friuli Pinot Grigio DOC
description: Step beyond ordinary Pinot Grigio with this delightful beauty from Venica & Venica's second label. This wine has a racy, refreshing profile. Immerse yourself in a whirlwind of crunchy fresh fruit flavors – Anjou pear, green apple, and a subtle touch of citrus zest. Elevating the everyday, this vibrant palate-pleaser redefines the standard for Pinot Grigio — and it’s soooooooooooo much better than most on the market.
